title: Decision-maker brief: Private deployments — auditability, control-plane framing, and competitive edges
content:
Purpose:
This brief is a compact decision-maker-facing narrative and competitive summary to use in 1:1s with CTOs, CISOs, and Compliance leads considering Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem). Aim: concise speaking points + objection-ready evidence and the short list of technical differentiators that matter in procurement discussions.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
Many regulated customers don’t need an opaque managed service — they need predictable inference economics, strong auditability, and clear ownership boundaries. Redwood Private offers a customer-controlled control plane option (managed control plane or customer-hosted control plane), explicit audit trails, and integrations for KMS/HSM and SIEM that let procurement and security teams map the product to existing compliance frameworks. Positioning: “Bring the Redwood runtime into your network; retain control of keys, audit, and traffic flows while keeping the same API and operational tooling teams love.”

Primary decision-maker messages (short):
- CTO: predictable performance + same APIs across hosted and private reduces engineering lift. Callout: can pin model versions and rollout policies independent of cloud provider upgrades.
- CISO: data never leaves your network unless you opt in; keys remain in your KMS; audit logs shipped to your SIEM. Callout: optional customer-hosted control plane for environments that require no external control-plane traffic.
- Compliance Officer: mappings to SOC2 controls, data residency options, and an install checklist for auditors. Provide sample evidence (retention policy, audit log schema).
- Platform/Infra Lead: flexible deployment topologies (VPC peering, private link, on-prem air-gapped bundle), autoscaling knobs with capacity guarantees for Dedicated customers.

Precise control-plane language (framing options to use in convo):
- Managed private control plane: Redwood operates control-plane services in a private tenancy while customer-owned compute stays in the VPC. Minimal external network egress; Redwood access limited by firewall rules and customer IAM.
- Customer-hosted control plane: full control-plane components run in customer environment (Kubernetes/VMs). Redwood provides images, Helm charts, and upgrade guidance; no control-plane telemetry leaves the VPC unless explicitly enabled.
- Data plane vs control plane: Data plane (inference requests and model artifacts) lives in customer network. Control plane (orchestration, rollout state) is configurable — emphasize separation and options.

Top buyer objections and concise rebuttals (ready-to-say lines + evidence to attach):
1) "How do I prove model inputs/outputs aren’t shared?"
   - Rebuttal: We support S3-compatible private model stores and encrypted KV caches; we can enable write-only telemetry and provide per-request hashes for audit.
   - Evidence: sample audit log, example retention policy, deployment pack with model-store config.
2) "We can’t accept any external API calls for control or telemetry."
   - Rebuttal: Offer customer-hosted control plane or a managed control plane with strict egress firewalling and allowlisting; telemetry can be disabled or forwarded to customer SIEM only.
   - Evidence: network diagram, configuration snippet that disables outbound telemetry, redaction settings doc.
3) "How do you handle key management?"
   - Rebuttal: Integrates with customer KMS/HSM (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, on-prem HSM); we store zero plaintext keys and support BYOK flow.
   - Evidence: KMS integration guide, threat model excerpt.
4) "What about model provenance and change control?"
   - Rebuttal: Model catalog with immutable model-version IDs, rollout policy timelines, canary windows and audit trail of every model change.
   - Evidence: sample model-catalog export and an audit timeline CSV.
5) "If we run on-prem, who supports upgrades and incident response?"
   - Rebuttal: We offer several support tiers: remote ops (access-controlled), partner-managed packages, or fully self-managed with runbooks. SLA-backed upgrade windows available on enterprise contracts.
   - Evidence: support matrix, sample runbook.

Competitive calls-to-action (what to show/say):
- Demo: provision a temporary VPC deployment that shows model pinning, a rolling canary, and audit logs forwarded to Splunk or Datadog.
- Proof: hand over a SOC2 artifacts checklist and a one-page network diagram template the customer can give to their network team.
- Pilot: 30-day pilot with realistic throughput and a single production route to validate latency and cost numbers.

Quick competitive differentiators (one-line bullets vs typical alternatives):
- Public cloud hosted endpoints: Redwood matches API simplicity but adds explicit control-plane options and audit-first telemetry designed for compliance reviews.
- Self-built inference stacks: Redwood provides the kernel/runtime work (KV cache, dynamic batching, quantization recommendations) so customers avoid months of performance tuning and unpredictable unit economics.
- Other inference vendors: Redwood couples observability and rollout tooling (per-route token cost, regressions tied to evals) with private deployment options; not just a binary self-host vs managed choice.

Evidence artifacts to attach in a customer package (recommended):
- One-page network diagram templates for the 3 deployment modes
- Control-plane option comparison (matrix)
- KMS/HSM integration guide and BYOK checklist
- Sample audit log (anonymized) and retention policy
- Small compliance pack: SOC2 mapping, data residency statement, sample DPA clause

Technical annex (short bullets that buyers ask for):
- Audit log schema: request-id, route, model-version, timestamp, request-hash, response-hash, user-id (if provided), operator-actions (model-promotion/rollback).
- Telemetry: optional outbound telemetry; forward-only to customer SIEM over TLS; can be disabled entirely.
- Connectivity patterns: VPC peering, private-link, reverse-proxy (customer egress only), and air-gapped install with removable media.
- Keys: supports envelope encryption, HSM-backed master keys, automatic key-rotation harmonized with customer KMS.
- Upgrades: cluster upgrade redline (canary control-plane first, then staggered runtime updates), rollback safepoints recorded in audit logs.

Short sale scripts for common buyer profiles (one-liners):
- CTO: "You keep your keys and audit trails; we give you a production LLM runtime that behaves exactly like our hosted API so your engineering team can reuse the same integrations."
- CISO: "We offer a customer-hosted control plane and SIEM-forwarding so you retain forensic data and control of any telemetry."
- Compliance lead: "Here’s a mapping of our controls to SOC2 and the exact artifacts auditors ask for; we’ll run a dry audit checklist with you during the pilot."

Pricing/contract cues to use early:
- Emphasize predictable committed capacity for Dedicated deployments, with optional burst lanes for short peaks.
- Private pricing anchored on capacity (vGPU units) + support tier + optional enterprise features (retention, extended logs).

Open risks we should own proactively (internal):
- Expect deep network/security reviews; prepare tailored network diagrams and a checklist for common firewall rules.
- Customers will request penetration test results and occasional SOC2 scope adjustments; coordinate with security team early.
- On-prem upgrades are sensitive; keep a clear rollback story and offer a rehearse/upgrade-run pilot.

Action items for sales/SEs before next wave of demos: (owner tags)
- Produce a trimmed 1-page "control-plane options" PDF for buyers (Aisha).
- Create a demo kit with Splunk/Datadog forwarding and a pre-baked model store (Diego).
- Draft a short runbook for customer-hosted control plane installation (Leah).
- Coordinate with Security to make a template penetration-test evidence package (Sunil).

Appendix: suggested attachments to include in first outreach email to security/compliance:
- 1-page network pattern PDF, 1-page KMS integration note, SOC2 mapping CSV, and a link to an interactive demo request form.

Notes and open questions for the product team: (work in progress)
- Should we offer a hardened minimal telemetry mode as a product flag? (will reduce discussion friction).
- Can we produce a standardized sample audit log for each release to speed auditor review?
- Define the smallest-supported on-prem footprint for a valid production SLA.

End of brief.
